page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU profile. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction support for AVX-512 with VNNI. The hypervisor layer is Microsoft Hyper-V. By restricting the core allocation relative to the underlying 64-core chassis, the instance delivers a massive 504.0 GB of system memory, equating to 15.75 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage consists of 2577 GB of bundled local SSD space alongside support for premium remote storage. No discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this virtual machine, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. The balance of high RAM capacity, sizable local solid-state storage, and reduced core count makes this configuration strategically cost-effective for enterprise software that requires substantial memory footprints while operating under restrictive per-core licensing models.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid memory performance, led by a strong PassMark memory score of 2874.76 and uncached large-block memory write throughput of 94.63 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks fall within mid-tier performance bands, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10861.0, a PassMark CPU score of 29157.29, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 29805.05. Redis throughput achieves 28.0 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 21.68 GB/sec. Large model CPU inference is constrained, processing 70B parameter prompts at 5.54 tokens per second.

The Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v4 is best suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, heavy caching clusters, and analytics engines that prioritize memory density and fast local scratch storage over high CPU core concurrency.
